"Dearest Isobel,” the newly transformed woman addressed her, head tilted in an owlish manner. “Selûne guides you, does she not?”
Isobel nodded, gesturing toward her embroidered Selûnite robes. “I am a cleric of the Moonmaiden, yes. With forms such as yours, I assume you have a connection to Her as well?”
Aylin beamed down at Isobel, her pale blue eyes sweltering with joyous intensity. “I am Dame Aylin, the undying Sword of the Moonmaiden, Her daughter and Her vengeance incarnate.”
Isobel’s eyes widened. She dropped down on one knee and swallowed heavily as all of the saliva in her mouth dried up. She could feel her heartbeat throughout her entire body, adrenaline coursing through her at the knowledge that the …owl knight? she’d been conversing with was Selûne’s very own daughter.

Reborn without the advantages of a prince’s wealth and status, he has only his paladin Oath to guide him as he struggles to lead a rag-tag group of misfits fighting an insidious cult that would unleash a terrible evil upon Faerûn.
Maekar Targaryen also died with unfinished business. The accidental killing of his brother stained Maekar’s soul with the curse of kinslaying, as well as a grief and guilt he was never able to heal before his own sudden violent death. Taken and twisted against his will by an evil god, Maekar is reborn in another world to become the unstoppable avatar of Murder, fated to end all existence…unless he can resist and defeat the Dark Urge within.
Destinies intertwined, Baelor and Maekar are bound to either save each other, or doom each other…and their new world along with them.

summary:
Like instinct, Astarion finds the vein in Filraen’s wrist that connects his fingers all the way to his heart. The moment his fangs sink into the Drow’s skin, blood pools into his mouth, and Astarion feels like a man drinking water for the first time in weeks.
He sucks and pulls, lapping at every drop with his tongue to make sure none goes to waste. Filraen’s blood tastes syrupy sweet tonight from the mead, thick and warm as it works its way down his throat. It’s addicting in more ways than one—the taste is divine, but something more primal pools in the lower parts of Astarion’s stomach. The kind that makes him want to bare his fangs at anyone who dares get too close to his Drow, that might try and take this away from him.
There’s a careful hand touching the base of his skull, pulling Astarion from his degenerating thoughts at the perfect moment. The long fingers slip up the back of his scalp and thread into his wavy hair like a soft caress. It’s comforting, has Astarion sighing wistfully into Filraen’s wrist.---

When the Solar Viryn breaks Heaven's oldest law to tear a death-god out of the world and free the souls he hoarded, he learns the law was never justice — only fear, wearing order's face. An age ago the overgod chained the great Serpent, froze the turning wheel of creation, and called the long stillness peace. Now the wheel is straining to turn, and every power in two pantheons is being drawn, by the truest part of its own nature, toward a war that serves a hand none of them can see.
Allied with a fallen angel who keeps a private count of the dead, Viryn fights from the Abyss to Asgard to the City of Judgment itself — toward a Ragnarok that will unmake the world the architects built and let a green one rise in its place. This ledger differs from the others. It is not theological, not academic, not even fully coherent. It is a witness account, a record of the time when Bane was dead, during the interregnum between the Time of Troubles and Bane’s return in 1372 DR.
Ceannas remained devout through the silence. He kept the rituals alive. He enforced tyranny without a master. And in the absence of Bane’s voice, he began to imagine what the return would look like. He theorized possession not because he feared it but because he longed for it.

series.name: Ledgers, Manuscripts, Books of All Sorts

title: Ledger III: The God-Touched and the Hollow by C Ceannas
author: Darkendsong
summary:
This ledger departs from C. Ceannas's earlier writings on devotion and pain, turning inward toward a subject he can neither fully understand nor ignore: those who have been touched by divinity and left changed by it.
Through a series of observations, confessions, and encounters with abandoned priests, failed vessels, and forsaken servants, Ceannas explores the spiritual wounds left behind when divine favor fades. He becomes increasingly fascinated by the idea that the greatest mark a god leaves upon a mortal is not power, but absence.
What begins as a study of others gradually becomes a study of himself.

series.name: Ledgers, Manuscripts, Books of All Sorts

title: Ledger II: The Doctrine of Dominion by C Ceannas
author: Darkendsong
summary: The second ledger of a series of ledgers written by a fervent follower of Bane, named C Ceannas. C Ceannas was very devout and it was assumed that he would be the Chosen of Bane during the second sundering, not some young upstart. This is his blueprint for tyranny. A mix of ideology, prophecy, and raw logistics. It is written in confident expectation that he would become the Chosen of Bane, not yet knowing that this young man quickly working up through the ranks would take the place that should rightfully (in his eyes) be his.

The Loviatar fanatic Abdirak is an… interesting diversion. He smells overwhelmingly of blood, fresh and old, feverishly sour in a way that delicately wrinkles Astarion's nose.

They stare at each other in a way that appears only marginally less intimate than the tadpoles linking their minds. [...]

He seems to adjust himself, and Astarion snorts quietly when he realizes that he's been getting off on this. The others either don't notice or are too polite to make it known. Perhaps he's making assumptions. But he's definitely not imagining the little smirk he catches when he and Eraad lock eyes.

title: Of old habits and festivals
author: anarchy_amaryllis
summary: The clearing buzzed with activity, laughter, clanging tools, a dozen voices overlapping in requests and half-formed questions. Leto stood in the center of it all, the eye of the storm, her jaw tight and her eyes darting between tasks. One hand gripped her ledger, the other kept brushing hair out of her face in restless, agitated motions. She hadn’t sat down all morning, hadn’t eaten, hadn’t even touched the tea Meg had pushed into her hands an hour ago.Her answers were shorter now. Crisper. She was still smiling, still sweet, but it was a blade-thin thing, too bright and too tight.Halsin had been watching from a distance, not hovering, but always near enough to step in if she stumbled. And she was starting to stumble. He stepped closer with a steady calm, voice low and teasing in the way that usually made her roll her eyes and smile.

title: Of honey and bears
author: anarchy_amaryllis
summary: Their life wasn’t as chaotic as she had initially believed. Caring for multiple children was exhausting, yet deeply rewarding. They were eager learners, constantly seeking new knowledge and asking her to teach them things to impress Daddy Halsin, the leader of their unusual community. She enjoyed her time with the other women in the community, learning how to sew and knit while training them at sword fighting and teaching them how to take care of the land they were living on, following some of Father Oak's teachings. Leto also loved her “me time” where she dedicated herself to refine her druid magic and her connections with Silvanus, sometimes forgetting to take breaks for eating something and keeping herself hydrated. She wasn’t used to it, always finding herself too immersed in her tasks to even feel the need to drink water or feed herself, her body never told her when to stop, too focused on the task at hand rather than her wellbeing. That was one of those days and Halsin was more than ready to help his lovely robin, his personal mission to keep her balanced more and more rooted in his soul.

title: Of emotions and comfort
author: anarchy_amaryllis
summary: Leto knew perfection was unnatural. It was a construct, something created as a diabolical ultimate goal. It was the hopeless desire to be flawless that tortured her since she was little, scarring her young soul permanently. Emptiness was her closest friend, a companion that followed her anywhere since she was around the age of eight. She grew used to feeling “that way” most of the days, she knew the tricks to make it go away, but each time the voice came back it was monstrously more powerful than the previous time.She wanted to live, but she was too tired to fight, too exhausted to defend herself from those voices.In that intense darkness, she could find the smallest hope that someday things would be better and she would desire to live again. That hope grew stronger the moment she had met her friends and Halsin.

Ten years have passed since defeating the Elder Brain and so very much has changed.
For the past five of those ten years The Matron, a well known figure in Baldur's Gate even before the mentioning of parasites, has lived her retirement from adventuring and the orphanage she ran in near complete seclusion. Near complete, if not for the occasional visits from her lovers, Shadowheart and Halsin.
She has kept her new life as secret from all others as much as possible, even going to the extreme lengths of faking her own death so that no one would dare look for her. All this to escape her past lover, Astarion, The Vampire Ascendant.

title: Midnight Bloom
author: OldGodsFavoritePrincess
summary:
The Netherbrain is defeated, and Minthara Baenre finds herself oddly disappointed. She should be celebrating with the vagabonds and strays she aligned herself with, right? Savouring her vengeance on the cult that wronged her, with their blood still fresh on her tongue and matted in her hair, but instead, she feels cold and empty—and she can’t help but notice a particular Cleric has a matching empty look in her eyes, too.
Everyone around her is celebrating, and yet the moment feels strangely reminiscent of the day Shadowheart and her friends danced and sang with the tieflings in the Emerald Grove. Once again, Shadowheart feels adrift and confused, the wine working its way into her veins and numbing the dread for what is to come tomorrow. She has no family and little faith to guide her, and everyone else seems to have a plan for what's next—everyone else but Minthara.

tags: But Only For Gale and Durge
summary:
It's been a couple of days after the crash of the Nautiloid.
Gale, Durge, and Astarion scout the beach for clues and anything of use as they still try to understand and adjust to their situation and the odd team they make.
All's well, as far as the circumstances allow, until an ambush from a devil in the shadows.
One fist fight later, the ambush turned out to be a regular run-in, and the devil is not a devil at all, just a surprisingly tall and grim-looking tiefling who introduces himself as D'ylân, the wandering bard and fellow survivor of the kidnapping and crash. Just a regular drifter with a flair for the dramatic when it suits him and a winning smile.
But it isn't until another encounter where D'ylân is mistaken for a devil that he agrees to join the trio, much to the delight of Gale, the appreciation of Durge, and the horror of Astarion. Where others see a potential friend and ally, the alleged elf sees nothing but danger and a threat.
In short: A turbulent beginning of D'ylân and Astarion's Sanguine Sonata love story that is all story and little love at first.

The camp was silent.No one spoke. Nothing moved. Not even the birds called from the trees.
Shadowheart stood half-donned in her armour, dragged from her tent by shouts of alarm. Her mace hung loose in her grip. She stood at the edge—at the edge of a puddle of blood so thick it still hadn’t dried in the morning sun. It crept across the sand in sluggish veins, seeping into the lake until the water ran red.
She numbly watched a lute string drift there, its pale surface dulled and sticky with gore. The bard’s body lay crumpled beside Isha’s discarded hunting knife—the one thing she had carried from before the Nautiloid—its blade slick with blood. Her eyes were still wide in the scream that marked her end.Her stomach had been torn open, stabbed until it was nothing but blood, bone, and pulp.
Shadowheart supposed it had been inevitable. Isha had tried to warn them. All of them. Time and time again.And only now, when it was far, far too late, did Shadowheart understand.They hadn’t failed to hear her.They had simply never listened.

 Thunder followed the lightning so fast this time, he thought it might strike near him. A gleeful giggle escaped him. Dad would be mad, but this was worth it. The river needed the company.
Sometimes he felt bad for it.
So much anger in it, that it couldn't be contained. A strength that nothing would stop. It grew, and grew, until it destroyed everything in its path. And the farmers would curse the river. The people whose homes had been overrun by the waters would curse the river. Anybody who had lost land, loved ones, or possessions to the raging flow would curse the river.
But he knew. It wasn't its fault.
And so whenever the river was overtaken by the anger of the skies, he ran to the shore to whisper in the middle of the tempest. "I understand. I understand, it's alright."

You have fond memories of visiting your aunt in Baldur’s Gate when you were a child. She wrote to you often, detailing the action as the Army of the Absolute approached, the destruction of the city when chaos erupted one morning as a giant brain rose above the masonry, and then the rebuilding efforts after the dust had settled.
Her letters were hopeful at first as the “great and good of Baldur’s Gate” stepped up to rebuild, but soon the tone changed. She told you that the city was being rebuilt into something… different. Something sinister, shadowed by a pall of mist and fear. Her disheveled scribblings whispered of a darkness that had risen within the walls.

summary:
He crawled back to camp, stomach knotting itself with hunger, nearly doubling over from the pain, the need. He was thankful that no one had been badly injured that day - no scent of blood lingering in the air to drive him deeper into desperation.
He was also thankful that Jen hadn't questioned him putting his tent a distance from the others, though he barely had enough energy to grab his bedroll and drag it inside. He collapsed into the middle of the assorted blankets and pillows he'd accumulated, burying his face in them.
After a long moment, Astarion turned over so he was laying on his back, and settled his breathing into a routine pattern. Maybe, hopefully, reverie would let him ignore his hunger for a few hours.
--
It's been nine days since Astarion found freedom via a tadpole in his brain and being dumped in the wilderness. Nine days since he tagged along with people that were either annoyingly kind or annoyingly secretive.
Nine days of near-constant travel, combat and hunting animals for food. Nine days of slow, crippling exhaustion and a lack of enough blood to sustain him.
Nine days of being tormented by the memory of a drop of Jen's blood, and he was desperate.

title: Anatomy of hunger
author: stop_licking_the_damn_thing
summary:
Camillius wakes on a ruined shore with sand in his lungs and fire in the sky. The wreck of the nautiloid smolders behind him, spilling corpses and smoke into the sea. In his skull, something moves — a parasite, a curse he knows far too much about. Scholars write of ceremorphosis in half-mad fragments, but Camillius has read them all, and knowledge is no comfort. It only tells him how little time he has left.
He means to survive with dignity, to cling to the healer’s oath buried in his bones. But the companions he finds are anything but simple: a cleric with secrets clenched in her fists, a githyanki soldier whose blade bites before her words, and above all—Astarion.
Astarion, who smiles too easily, who circles like a predator, who makes mockery of fear. His beauty is cruel, his hunger unmistakable, and Camillius cannot look away. He tells himself he is observing, cataloguing, studying the stranger the way one might study venom beneath glass. But every hour draws him closer, and every glance cuts deeper.
This is not a simple love story. It is a study in hunger, in power, and in the unbearable gravity of being seen.

When she woke up on that Nautiloid with an empty past and an insistent Urge, she didn't know quite what to make of it. Night after night, into darkness she crept, thinking she was sneaky while her master slept, but as she tore through bloody muscle and bone, her master sat by the fire, waiting alone. For the cat always awoke as their bed turned cold, but the mouse could keep her silence - he had an agreement to uphold. Then one night, she didn’t come back, and though she’d been his darkness, his world turned to black. He thought he understood what she so frequently said - when her bloodlust stirs, she always dreams in red. He swore he’d find her and bring her back home, but the cat had to be mindful of her father's throne. When he finally found her abandoned and lost, he thought that the parasite was the only cost, but soon he realized her memories were gone, and with them, their past, their love, their bond.

summary: Astarion was focused on Halsin's hand still on her shoulder. It twisted something in his stomach that he didn't acknowledge. Her story was one of hardships and war, and yet she was the kindest soul he'd ever met. It made him… angry. And he didn't know why.The rest of the night passed with lighter conversations, until a watch was established. And Ursa didn't ask to talk after the others had gone to sleep. She didn't come into his tent and ask to sleep together, to touch him, to pry. She made sure the fire was tended, wished him goodnight with a smile, and went to start her watch and that was it.Maybe he'd lost the privilege to know her heart.He told himself that he would be fine with that. Obviously, he would be. He didn't care about any of these people outside of the protection they offered him. And he was fine with that: better yet, that's what he wanted from these assorted freaks. That was his goal from the start.He stared, seething and scowling at the roof of his tent.Why was he so mad about this?

Everyone is a little weird, but they all need to work together to get through this mess. Between a wizard that might blow up, an elf who might eat the party, the cleric and fighter snipping at each other, a monster hunter and a woman who didn't end up a monster after all, things are not off to a great start. title: Baldur’s Gate: A novelization

summary:
———
Gale was at the head of the pack. He’d suggested he could tell the direction of civilization by sensing the movements of the weave. The dragonborn doubted it but said nothing. He was too busy devouring a jar of pickled fish he’d found in the looters tent and eyeing Astarion, who was behaving strangely.
The elf was walking farther off, alongside them, weaving in and out of trees, meandering between honey-gold rays of sunlight pouring down through the canopy. He stared up at the light and seemed to hardly be watching where he was going, only occasionally glancing over to them when he drifted too far away.
———
This is an ongoing novelization of the game. My aim is to give more detail and weight to events, story beats, character arcs, and all those things that we normally have to ignore because of video game reason: characters staying at camp, Withers reviving people, companions having little to say to each other, etc.

title: Blood Becomes Water

tags: Redemption with a lot of work involved
summary:
With the Absolute vanquished, the disinherited godchild finds herself, for the first time, alone. If she was going to be haunted by the sins of her past, she preferred to know what those sins were. In exchange for a piece of her soul, Withers agrees to bring back someone who claimed to know those sins better than anyone — Enver Gortash.
  
    "That person you once knew… I don't think there's any bringing them back, either — not in the way you knew them."
  
  
    She paused, thinking back on the few months her meager memory could retain. Someone had always been there to direct her — to a better or worse path, she couldn't always say. But they had pushed her forward at least. Always forward.
  
  
    "I've changed," she said.
  
  
    A shadow of pain passed ever so briefly on Gortash's face, then it was gone. He put on that practiced and easy smile — the same one he wore to patriars' balls and deals with devils alike.
  
  
    "Then I'll simply have to get to know you all over again," said Gortash.

title: Trust Me, Darling - The Prologue
author: ms_fahey
summary: The year is 1300DR, and Astarion Ancunín awakens in a coffin, driven by a compulsive urge to escape and find Lord Cazador Szarr. Astarion, scared of the unknown fate that awaits him on the Fugue Plane, chooses immortality and accepts the vampire's dark gift. It is only later that he learns how long eternity will be - and how Cazador intends to use the beautiful young lawyer to feed his insatiable lust for power, control ... and blood.***“Are you here to claim my gift?” Cazador asked from atop his throne. “Will you embrace immortality, my son? You have tasted death once – how did you like it?”Astarion bowed his head, terror soaring through him. He wasn’t even forty, still an elf-child - he thought he had so much more time to make his mark on the world, earn his place in the kingdom of one God or another. The memory of dimming blackness, the idea of being trapped on the Fugue Plane, his soul unclaimed for eternity, made him shake. All he wanted was one last chance, to survive, to live.“I accept,” he choked out, not really knowing what he was agreeing to – but it didn’t matter. Anything to escape his fate.“Then you shall be mine,” Cazador said, rising slowly. “Forever.”

summary:
It's Bite Night. Only Luka Morrigan (Tav) is a dhampir from Barovia, and he can bite back. 
Also known as "In Which Astarion Tastes What a Well-Adjusted Family Looks Like and Has a Breakdown About It."All goes quiet in the camp, the night is still. 
Astarion waits for another hour, tracing his favorite patterns in the stars to be sure Luka is fully asleep. Then he makes his approach. 
He finds Luka curled over on his side, head resting on hands that are folded as if in prayer. Overly moral indeed—a right proper stick-in-the-mud. In four days of traveling together, despite running into bandits and goblins and an entire caravan of refugee tieflings, the boy has never raised his voice. He shows kindness to everyone and always chooses to help others before he helps himself. It’s sickening. Helping yourself is a luxury Astarion hasn’t been allowed in centuries. 
Who could’ve possibly sired such a soft creature?

    ”We do not have time to help this… ‘ambulance’. We must report directly to my Kith’rak.” asserted the green one.
  
  
    “We are in need of aid ourselves, perhaps you can travel with us until we find a healer,” said the purple one.

Gale’s life is quiet and predictable, spent working at the library and having quiet evenings with his cat- when he’s not dealing with his insufferable neighbor, Astarion.That is until he wakes up in a world of magic and danger, where he knows nothing and no one, except for one constant: Astarion is still there, sharper, deadlier, and just as much of an asshole.Now Gale has to survive a story he doesn’t belong in, with no plan, no knowledge of magic, and no idea how to get home.

summary:
Nearly a year has passed since she turned her back on Crèche D’riluth, her name dragged through both blood and ruin. Exile was supposed to be freedom from blood-wrought zealotry. Instead, Cy’ra find herself wandering the streets of Baldur’s Gate, loneliness stalking her like a cruel shadow, haunted by the silver glow of a goddess she was never meant to reach for. Noise is all she seeks—something to drown the hollow aching in her chest where greatness once lived.
She finds Shadowheart instead: striking emerald eyes, a hand seared with Shar’s cruelty, and a hatred with an edge sharp enough to execute. She hadn’t expected her salvation to come dressed as violence, nor hatred to feel so close to home.
Brutality binds them first, and mercy keeps them near. Make them hunted. And as bounties rise and the gods snap their jaws, exile and acolyte alike will learn what it means to be pursued together—what it costs to bare their scars beneath Selûne’s unwavering gaze. They’ll be forced to choose: devotion, betrayal, or something far more dangerous, each other.
They’ll both be nobody’s soldier.

summary:
“Wait.”
 
Dolthedir stopped after only taking a step, Astarion’s weary voice drawing him to an immediate halt.
“Stay.”
Dolthedir stayed. He turned slowly back around to see that Astarion still had yet to move, but those last two words had been unmistakable. Dutifully, he knelt back down by the tub, resting his arms against the lip again. “All right. I’ll stay.”
They were both silent for several long moments, Astarion sitting in the warmed bath and Dolthedir kneeling beside him before Astarion finally moved. He lifted his right hand from the water, the thick coat of blood that had covered it so completely now broken up into thick streaks of dark red. “It isn’t coming off,” he said lamely, lifting his other hand to half-heartedly scrub at the back of his hand. “It’s still there.”After killing Cazador, Dolthedir (Tav) and the party return to the Elfsong Tavern to clean up and rest. title: You Want the World and You Know It
author: Chronurgy
summary:
Without any real thought Gale curled his fingers to summon a magical flame, instinctually seeking some bit of light and heat and life to accompany him in this desolate place. Nothing answered his call; the spell smothered in its crib with cold, slick fingers. Though nothing changed, he felt colder, even more unwelcome. He had tried to bring vitality to a place antagonistic to the concept, and in doing so drawn whatever wrath this place might manifest further down upon himself. There were no shadows here, lit as it was by a constant, unknowable source of light. But he felt hemmed in by hungry shadows all the same.
He kept walking. He did not know what else to do.
And in between one step and the next, just as surely as there had been nothing, there was something. Two figures equidistant, not far from him, both still.
One he knew, and one he did not.

A contract had ensured a path to this victory, the Orphic Hammer freeing a vital ally that opened Death's Door wide for the wizard to triumph over their shared enemy...but by this single selfless act of destruction, he had also broken the deal by destroying the promised artifact.And now Raphael wants his dues.-
  “Have you nothing to say for yourself, Gale of Waterdeep?” Raphael growled, his impatience with the silence becoming more than he could contain.
  Patience was the centuries of preparation, of planning.
  Patience was the horde of souls manipulated into his bidding over countless generations.
  Patience was the precise timing, finally moving his pieces across the board.
  Patience had disappeared along with the Crown.

title: Tetrad
author: TheBlindBandit
summary:
Selûnite chants are calming, circular, cyclical, the ebb and flow of them wonderfully meditative. Isobel follows along, but for once in her life she feels like she is swimming against the rush of the tide. Wouldn't it be such a boon for Aylin, her mind insists stubbornly, such an undeniable reassurance.
  The mounting power is palpable, as if there are far more than three priestesses leading the ritual, as if there are hundreds and hundreds of faithful joining in, even thousands, perhaps; an entire sea right alongside the few dozen gathered here.
  At the end of it, between one blink and the next, she is there—a Shard of Selûne in the luminous flesh.
The Conjuring of the Second Moon is performed every four years, in the midst of summer, on the leap day of Shieldmeet. Four years - a long and a short time.Four different Shieldmeets in Aylin's and Isobel's lives.

author: stendhal
summary:
He walks, eyes half-shut, and thinks about:
  New York City, all those decades ago—skylights, fine jewels, designer clothes and Broadway shows; he thinks about:
  London, all those centuries ago—cold Aprils, the clack-click-clomp of horse-drawn carriages on cracked cobblestone, dear sweet Sebastian; and now: now, he has:
  Los Angeles: home to real stars, real wealth and the city’s own brand of filth that lives in the putrid grime buried beneath the glitz and glamour.
It's been a good night, but there'll be more: days, nights, years, decades.

He’d seduce her, romance her, make her feel like she was the only girl in the world. And after he had given her the night of her life, positively ruined her for anyone else, he’d begin whispering in her ear. He’d become her lover, her confidant. And then she would become his puppet. That was more than a fair trade. He’d have a gorgeous meal, his space would be guaranteed in their little group, at the top where he belonged, and then somehow, he didn’t know how, but, somehow, Tav would waltz their merry band back to Baldur’s Gate and drive a stake right through Cazador Szarr’s heart. For him. Afterwards, well, Tav had served her purpose. Then he could truly do as he pleased.Astarion smiled a wide, real smile and finished his wine, wincing at the cheap, bitter taste.At that moment Tav looked up from her supplies and caught him staring. He raised his empty goblet to her and she waved back, a warm smile softening her lovely features.This was going to be so easy.

title: he was black sheep and mischief and love for his craft

summary:
“If you were to ask me, that spitfire temper of yours is worth more than two gold,” Raphael hums, eyes low as they drag against his face. There’s enough innuendo on that fake face of Raphael’s to put the finest whore at Sharess’ Caress to shame.
  “Is that so?” he asks, squints. “Excuse me if I’m a little skeptical, darling. It’s rather hard to put much weight into the opinion of a demon, you see.”
  “Oh, don’t be so harsh,” Raphael says, tilting his head. “I’ll have you know that I am so much more than those filthy, savage worms that crawl around in the Abyss.”
  “Ah, how idiotic of me. Devils, demons, yes, I see the difference now, thank you,” he says, jabbing his finger as hard as he can into Raphael’s... unusually firm forearm. Ridiculous. Devils don’t need defined muscles. “Which brings me the question I am cursed to ask you each and every time you find your way to this carnival, and more importantly, to my booth. Why. Are. You. Here?”
Even in a city as horrid as Baldur’s Gate, it’s a lovely night for a carnival.

Astarion slinked around Gale where he sat behind his desk doing his various little wizardly things. “I’ve been studying.”
 
  Gale’s face lit up. “That’s excellent news! I’m of the opinion that one should take every opportunity to expand their knowledge. What, uh—” Astarion had leaned over his shoulder, just daring his heart to race. He continued with a much smaller voice, “What subject have you taken up?”

You saved me – now let me help you” you get up tugging on his hand.“Stubborn little thing, aren’t you?” he grunts but gets up with you “One might think you’re the one starving here” he adds with a seductive smile.“Just be quiet” you pull him closer as you lean back onto a stone plated cabinet.He stares into your eyes for a long moment, then finally gives in.He moves slowly this time. Carefully. One hand brushes your hair back, fingers lingering at your jaw. The other steadies your shoulder as he leans in. When his lips graze your skin, it’s not like before. There’s no rush. No frenzy. Just cold breath. His mouth carefully clasps your neck and he lingers there for a while- silent, still.

What began as a reluctant friendship became something deeper. Two young elves, fumbling through their first brush with affection beneath the suffocating weight of duty and expectation. But before that fragile bond could become anything more, politics and betrayal tore them apart.
Two hundred years later, their paths cross again. Astarion no longer remembers the girl who once stole his book and his heart. Eleni remembers everything.
This is the story of what came before. Of love left unsaid, of threads never truly severed. A tale of missed chances, fractured memories, and a bond that survives even death.

At the edge of the Shadow-Cursed lands, the party takes refuge in the Last Light Inn—but the darkness outside is nothing compared to the storm brewing within. Tav is unraveling.
Haunted by urgency, guilt, and the unbearable weight of leadership, she lashes out at her companions, jeopardizing fragile alliances and driving a wedge into the heart of the group. When a confrontation explodes into violence, it’s Astarion—calm, cold, and furious—who takes a stand.
What follows is not seduction. It’s not comfort. It’s reckoning.
Behind closed doors, Tav is stripped down—emotionally and physically—until her walls finally crack. In the aftermath of fierce correction and fierce love, she must face her companions and ask the hardest question of all:

summary: In the quiet exile of a borrowed tower, Gale seeks solace in study—until a book finds him instead. In the timeless halls of the Library of Toth, he discovers a volume bound in midnight-dyed hide and sealed with Mystra’s mark. Its pages unravel a version of his goddess he had never been meant to know: Ariel Manx, a mortal girl who rose too quickly, ascended too young, and ruled a domain she barely understood.What begins as curiosity becomes revelation. The divine image Gale once worshipped fractures into something human—fallible, frightened, and far less omniscient than she appeared. Through her forgotten mortal history, he begins to see the patterns: the chosen used, the faithful discarded, the love never truly returned.This is the chapter where reverence gives way to reckoning. Where a man who once loved a goddess begins to grieve the girl she used to be—and the truth that neither of them were ever free.

summary:
Withers’ final words whispered through the hollow cavern of her being, settling deep in the marrow of her bones.
“He will come for thee, again and again, until his will is fulfilled—until the ritual is complete, as it was always written. For in all things, death is thy gift.”Tav disappeared the moment the battle was won. No goodbyes, no explanations, just silence where she once stood. The Dark Urge was never truly gone, and she knew if she stayed, ruin would follow.
Two years have passed.
Baldur’s Gate is on its way to being Astarion’s city now, shaped beneath his power as the Vampire Ascendant. He is everything he once longed to be. The past should remain buried, but it never does—not when the streets run red once more, not when the Cult of Bhaal rises from the shadows.
Astarion moves to crush them, not just to solidify his rule, but for revenge. For what they took from him. But when he finds her again, he realizes the terrible truth. She never left to escape him. She left to protect him. And now, she’s his to save.
But destinies are written in blood, and even love may not be enough to rewrite them.

summary:
With this new sensation, this beautiful sight, he has been distracted from noticing something was missing.
  Something has been absent since the worm entered his eye.
  The voice, Cazador’s voice. It’s gone.
  It’s gone.
  It’s gone.
  Astarion reels up to his feet, stumbling on the uneven ground in his fine shoes.
  Even in his dreams, even in the deepest of trances, Astarion can feel Cazador. The orders, the rules, that tug in his gut that pulls him, like a fish on a hook, back to the palace when he wanders too far. But it’s quiet.
  Astarion’s head has never had more physical occupants but has never been so quiet.
  His world hasn’t been this foreign in nearly 200 years, but that's what makes him realize with extreme clarity.
  Astarion is wide awake.
AKA: Astarion finds himself far from home, safer than he's been in centuries, yet in more danger than ever. summary: Senna saw her family.She saw Sarevok and Helena and Orin and the whole sorry lot of them. And Bhaal—always, always Bhaal. Her father. Her father, her shared flesh, and in any other world the sheer injustice of it would have rendered them all to dust. It should have. The world should never have allowed it. summary: My dearest Bhaalspawn,I received your gift. It was so thoughtful I nearly blushed. Jasper has never looked quite so lovely as he did cut up and arranged on my desk. title: to know the rain is falling
author: Raayide
tags: making grand steps insofar as how badly you can fuck up aftercare
the number one way to never get bored of your slave
summary:
He presses a hand to his chest. Feels bone, bird-thin, protruding through his skin. Dust. The box is stone and he is stone alongside, fossilized, drawn back to a life he cannot remember. The elf—Cazador—sire—master—pulls him from the dark. Says things that should be known but are not. Calls to him. Says come back.
  His voice trembles. It is barely a whisper. "Who am I?"
When he is laid to rest, he is full of history. When he wakes, there is very little left.
